text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Six solar farms of National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED), daylight hours, March 2024 to April 2026. IFS: ECMWF's forecast via Open-Meteo. Purple dot: that variable set's mean absolute error, pooled over lead days 1 to 3. Hollow diamond: the error of the row below, which is the zero of this row's step. Orange line: 95% interval of that step alone, from resampling whole months, drawn from the diamond. An orange line is not the uncertainty of its dot's position. A minus sign in the right column means the error fell. A step depends on the order in which the groups were added. A variable set is the list of inputs the XGBoost model is given, beside sun position and calendar. F0: IFS radiation and air temperature. Each set adds to the one before. F1: total cloud cover. F2: low, mid, and high cloud cover. F3: direct radiation. F4: dew point, column water vapour, boundary-layer height. F5: convective energy (CAPE), inhibition, visibility. F6 (all 20 IFS variables): surface and weather variables. IFS: ECMWF's 9 km forecast, 00 UTC run, read at a lead day. Exploratory: not named in the study plan before any result existed, and not corrected for multiple comparisons.'
text.tspan: Six solar farms of National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED), daylight hours, March 2024 to April 2026. IFS:
Purple dot: that variable set's mean absolute error, pooled over lead days 1 to 3.
Hollow diamond: the error of the row below, which is the zero of this row's step.
Orange line: 95% interval of that step alone, from resampling whole months, drawn from the diamond. An orange line
is not the uncertainty of its dot's position.
A minus sign in the right column means the error fell. A step depends on the order in which the groups were added.
A variable set is the list of inputs the XGBoost model is given, beside sun position and calendar.
F0: IFS radiation and air temperature. Each set adds to the one before. F1: total cloud cover. F2: low, mid, and
high cloud cover. F3: direct radiation. F4: dew point, column water vapour, boundary-layer height. F5: convective
energy (CAPE), inhibition, visibility. F6 (all 20 IFS variables): surface and weather variables.
IFS: ECMWF's 9 km forecast, 00 UTC run, read at a lead day.
Exploratory: not named in the study plan before any result existed, and not corrected for multiple comparisons.
